newsitem.title: USA: East St. Louis, Ill., faces $1 mln shortfall.
newsitem.headline: East St. Louis, Ill., faces $1 mln shortfall.

text.p: East St. Louis, an Illinois town that once faced possible bankruptcy, is now facing a $1 million shortfall in its upcoming fiscal year budget, the city's financial oversight official said Tuesday.

Bruce Patterson, executive director of the East St. Louis Financial Advisory Authority, said budget requests from city departments are running $1 million more than expected revenues for the fiscal year that begins Jan. 1.
Patterson said the city's accounting firm has recommended the layoff of 35 employees to bring the upcoming $18 million budget into balance.
The city is scheduled to present a proposed budget to the authority on Nov. 1.
"Whether we find (the budget) meets all the criteria is another question," Patterson said. "Before the whole issue is done, there will be a balanced budget."

A 1990 Illinois law tailored for East St. Louis' financial troubles created the authority to oversee the city's finances. The authority will continue to approve the city's budget, payments and contracts until the city ends 10 consecutive years with a balanced budget, according to Patterson.
So far, East St. Louis has completed three years of balanced operations, he said.

A $21 million 1994 bond issue backed by Illinois' moral obligation pledge enabled the city to restructure its debt. In addition, the arrival of a riverboat casino injected a new stream of revenue into the city's coffers.

However, the city's share of tax revenues from the casino, which opened in June 1993, is showing signs of stagnation, according to Patterson. He said estimated revenues for fiscal 1997 from the casino should remain at the fiscal 1996 level of $10 million.
"So the days of rising revenue and greater discretion of spending are ending now," he added.
